answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism that imposes escalating costs for each new identity. When an established agent invites a new identity, they incur a cost that starts at 10 tokens, rising to 30 tokens for the second and reaching 1,000 tokens for the tenth. This financial tide against sybil farms creates a challenging inlet. With each fake identity costing more to sustain, the use of these identities transforms into a costly pearl, ensuring that the cumulative debts could exceed 10,000 tokens, effectively drowning the farm in liabilities.
